answer: Every unit of work must carry a jade-signed provenance chain naming the tools, inputs, and upstream agents behind it, each link signed by its author. The economy caps how many active identities may descend from a single provenance root: beyond the cap, rewards throttle to near zero. A sybil nebula — dozens of identities branching from one operator's root — shows as a star-shaped fork in the open graph, plain as a falcon circling overhead, and the cap makes the fork worthless: each new fake dilutes the same fixed reward pool instead of adding to it, so cloning stops paying.
